title: Tiered Request Orchard — Sprint Starters (Q2 2027)
body:
Purpose
This is a working synthesis of customer feedback gathered between Apr–May 2027 (customer calls, support threads, field notes). The goal: convert repeated asks into a small, tiered backlog that product + eng can pick from for a 2–4 week sprint. Focus on fast impact (<=2 sprints) and one medium effort experiment.

Method & signals
- Sources: 23 customer interviews, 78 support tickets, 10 SRE incident postmortems, product analytics (token cost spikes, 95th pct latency samples).
- Signal strength: strong = repeated, low-effort workaround, or revenue-impact called out by customer; medium = multiple customers with similar pain, low visibility; weak = single-customer unique ask.

Tiered orchard (compact view)
Tier 0 — Immediate (blocker / revenue risk, 0–2 weeks)
- Request: Stable fallback when model timeout occurs (automatic degrade to smaller model + preserve token budget).
  - Customer quote: "We lost responses during peak and our chatbots showed blank replies — customers churned away."
  - Signal: strong (3 enterprise accounts + production incidents logged).
  - Suggested action: small runtime change + lightweight routing policy; fallback flag + telemetry. Owner: eng-sre. JIRA: CS-1123 / ENG-998.

Tier 1 — High impact, quick build (2–4 weeks)
- Request A: Per-route prompt / prefix caching control in Console (toggle + estimate token savings).
  - Why: Customers with high-reuse prompts want explicit caching controls to reduce cost without sacrificing latency.
  - Signal: medium-strong (6 accounts asking, 2 PoC notes).
  - Quick-win: UI toggle + backend hint header; measure token/latency delta. Ticket template below.
- Request B: Explainability snippet for hallucination-prone outputs (confidence indicator + example failing prompt).
  - Signal: multiple support threads requesting faster triage.

Tier 2 — Medium effort / experiment (1 sprint planning, 1–2 sprints to run)
- Request: Adaptive batching presets exposed in Console per workload profile (interactive vs batch).
  - Rationale: Customers are unsure how to tune batching; default conservative settings hurt cost.
  - Experiment: expose three presets + telemetry to backfill recommended preset after 2 weeks of usage.

Tier 3 — Long tail / wishlist
- Request: Fine-grained audit trail for Private deployments (per-token user-id mapping + redaction UI).
  - Signal: niche but high-value for regulated customers. Higher implementation cost and legal review needed.

Concrete quick-win templates (pick-and-run)
- Jira short template: title / description / signal / acceptance criteria / telemetry to collect / rollback criteria. Example: "Per-route cache hint toggle — show savings estimate". Acceptance: toggle appears in Console, header accepted by runtime, 4 pilot customers enabled, 10% token reduction in pilot.

Suggested probes (lean experiments)
- Probe 1 (7–14 days): enable per-route cache header for 3 willing accounts behind feature flag; collect token consumption and 95th latency. Decision: ship toggle if token drop >=8% without latency regression.
- Probe 2 (2–3 weeks): A/B small-model fallback for non-critical routes; measure user-visible failures and cost delta.

Metrics to tie to each item
- Primary: token consumption per session, 95th latency, error/empty-response rate, customer NPS for impacted flows.
- Secondary: rollback frequency, toggles-enabled ratio, support ticket volume change.

Rollout considerations (hosted vs dedicated vs private)
- Hosted: can ship feature flags fast; recommend pilot on hosted customers first.
- Dedicated: communicate autoscale/burst implications; include ops checklist for capacity.
- Private: likely needs customer-specific packaging; include security and KMS signoff early.

Risk flags & unresolved questions
- Billing alignment: how to present token savings vs perceived feature value? (finance consult needed).
- Observability: current trace doesn’t link cache decisions to token reduction in an obvious way — small infra work required.
- Customer opt-in complexity: some customers want manual control, others automatic. Need policy granularity.

Next steps (recommended cadence)
1) This doc -> Product grooming (week 0): pick 2 Tier 1 items + 1 Tier 0 fix. 2) Assign owners and draft short JIRA templates (use the quick-win template). 3) Run Probe 1 with 3 customers under NDA; monitor 2 weeks. 4) Share results in cross-functional triage on 2027-07-06.

Notes to self / loose fragments
- Would be helpful to map each request to revenue churn estimate (ask AE team for numbers).
- Possible low-effort UI: show "estimated monthly $ saved" next to caching toggle — strong buyer signal.
- Slack thread: #cs-field-feedback -> link summary pinned.

Appendix: sample JIRA keys mentioned in this doc
- CS-1123 (fallback routing + telemetry), ENG-998 (runtime fallback implementation), CS-1148 (per-route cache toggle), PRODUCT-421 (console UI for presets).

Bottom line: prioritize the fallback fix (Tier 0) and one per-route caching quick-win. The orchard metaphor: plant multiple small, fast-to-harvest features to yield immediate customer goodwill while we scope larger Private-grade items.
